digest.headline: Les modèles vidéo et les frameworks d'agents évolutifs dominent la veille IA avec des avancées en persistance, contrôle physique et standardisation des méthodes d'évolution.
digest.overview: La journée du 26 octobre 2026 met en lumière des progrès structurants en IA, notamment autour des architectures vidéo unifiées et des systèmes multi-agents. Les travaux sur l'interprétabilité, l'optimisation des LLM et les modèles embodied continuent de progresser, tandis que les benchmarks et frameworks standardisés gagnent en maturité pour évaluer et déployer ces technologies.

highlights.title: Unification des modèles vidéo autour de 4 opérations clés
highlights.text: Une synthèse propose de structurer les modèles vidéo (fondation et monde) autour de quatre opérations : lecture, écriture, partage et interaction. Cette approche souligne un shift vers des états persistants et un contrôle physique des environnements, plutôt qu'une simple amélioration de la fidélité perceptuelle. Elle offre un cadre théorique pour les architectures futures, notamment en robotique et simulation.

highlights.title: RSIHub : un framework standardisé pour l'évolution des agents
highlights.text: RSIHub introduit un framework open-source pour standardiser et comparer les méthodes d'évolution d'agents (prompts, outils, orchestration) via des recettes composables. Il permet d'instancier et d'évaluer des méthodes comme AHE ou Hyperagents sans modifier le cœur du système, avec des gains significatifs (jusqu'à 13,5 points en pass@1 sur MiniSWE et Terminal Bench 2). Ce travail répond au besoin croissant de reproductibilité et d'interopérabilité dans les architectures multi-agents.

highlights.title: Auto-amélioration des LLM et systèmes multi-agents hiérarchiques
highlights.text: Deux travaux marquants explorent l'auto-amélioration des LLM : l'un via une auto-distillation sur des paires QA synthétiques (sans supervision externe), l'autre via un système multi-agents hiérarchique entraîné end-to-end avec distillation sur politique. Ces méthodes démontrent des gains en efficacité et en résolution de tâches complexes, tout en réduisant la dépendance aux données annotées. Elles ouvrent des pistes pour l'optimisation autonome des modèles et la collaboration agentique.

highlights.title: Optimisation conjointe des poids neuronaux et modèles embodied unifiés
highlights.text: La représentation des poids neuronaux comme des chemins de décisions discrètes partagées (TWIG) unifie pruning, quantification et partage de poids, permettant une optimisation conjointe et une implémentation matérielle efficace. Parallèlement, RynnUnify propose un modèle embodied de 16B combinant compréhension visuelle et planification à long terme, avec des gains de 9,75 points en planification visuelle par rapport à Cosmos 3 Nano. Ces avancées illustrent une convergence entre optimisation des architectures et intégration multimodale.

highlights.title: Interprétabilité et évaluation des modèles
highlights.text: Un pipeline transforme les détecteurs de texte IA en classifieurs interprétables via des autoencodeurs parcimonieux, identifiant des traits linguistiques prédictifs et améliorant les performances hors distribution. Par ailleurs, RoboJudge et Dual Exam introduisent des benchmarks pour évaluer les MLLM en génération vidéo embodied et dissocier l'évaluation des agents et des modèles du monde. Ces travaux répondent aux enjeux de transparence et de robustesse, critiques pour les applications réglementées.

digest.trend: Les architectures IA évoluent vers une intégration plus poussée entre perception, action et mémoire, avec une emphase sur la standardisation des frameworks et l'autonomie des systèmes. Les modèles embodied et multi-agents gagnent en maturité, tandis que l'optimisation et l'interprétabilité deviennent des leviers clés pour des déploiements scalables et conformes.

items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.
items.tldr: Synthèse unifiée des modèles vidéo (fondation et monde) structurée autour de 4 opérations (lecture, écriture, partage, interaction), soulignant l'évolution vers des états persistants et un contrôle physique plutôt que la simple fidélité perceptuelle.

deep_analysis.probleme: Cette publication aborde le défi de l'unification des modèles de fondation vidéo et des modèles du monde vidéo sous une même perspective théorique. Le problème central réside dans la fragmentation des approches actuelles, qui traitent séparément la compréhension (lecture) et la génération (écriture) de vidéos, sans cadre cohérent pour modéliser les dynamiques sous-jacentes du monde réel qu'elles représentent. L'objectif est de proposer une taxonomie commune pour analyser ces modèles en termes de cohérence temporelle et de validité physique/causale, au-delà de la simple fidélité perceptuelle.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs adoptent une approche conceptuelle en structurant la littérature autour de quatre opérations complémentaires : 1) *Lecture* (inférer les propriétés du monde latent à partir de vidéos observées), 2) *Écriture* (générer des vidéos à partir de conditions spécifiées ou apprises), 3) *Partage* (intégrer compréhension et génération via des mécanismes de modélisation communs), et 4) *Interaction* (prédire et mettre à jour l'état du monde sous l'effet d'actions ou d'observations évolutives). Cette classification repose sur l'hypothèse que les vidéos sont des projections partielles et bruitées d'un monde latent temporel. Les détails techniques incluent une analyse des architectures (ex. : modèles de diffusion, transformeurs), des représentations (ex. : états latents, graphes causaux), et des benchmarks émergents pour évaluer la cohérence physique et la contrôlabilité.
deep_analysis.resultats: Le contenu disponible ne fournit pas de résultats quantitatifs ou de chiffres clés spécifiques, car il s'agit d'une *survey* (revue de littérature) plutôt que d'une étude expérimentale. Cependant, les auteurs identifient une tendance claire : un déplacement des priorités de la communauté vers des critères plus exigeants que la simple reconnaissance de clips ou la fidélité visuelle, tels que la persistance de l'état du monde, la validité causale, et l'évaluation via des interactions ou des décisions en aval. Ils soulignent aussi l'émergence de datasets et benchmarks dédiés à ces nouveaux défis (ex. : tests de cohérence physique ou de prédiction d'actions).
deep_analysis.limites: La principale limite de cette publication réside dans son caractère théorique et synthétique : elle propose un cadre unificateur sans valider empiriquement son applicabilité à tous les modèles existants. De plus, les défis identifiés (ex. : modélisation de la causalité, évaluation de la cohérence physique) restent largement ouverts et nécessitent des avancées techniques majeures. Enfin, le scepticisme est justifié quant à la capacité des modèles actuels à capturer des dynamiques mondiales complexes sans biais ou artefacts, surtout dans des scénarios interactifs ou non supervisés.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son effort de clarification conceptuelle et son potentiel à orienter les recherches futures vers des modèles vidéo plus robustes et interprétables, mais son impact concret dépendra de sa capacité à inspirer des implémentations pratiques et des benchmarks rigoureux.

items.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
items.summary: Agent-evolution methods use execution feedback to improve prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, but their implementations often rebuild the same experimental machinery. We present RSIHub, an open-source framework for building, comparing, and extending these methods on shared infrastructure. Recipes compose reusable operators and declare mutable resources; RSIHub supplies execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage. Researchers can focus on evolution policy while evaluation stays outside the mutable surface and results remain tied to candidates and evaluation conditions. We instantiate AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA without modifying the framework core, keeping method-specific logic in recipes and operators. We evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ^3 Banking under fixed model and evaluator configurations. The largest observed overall pass@1 gain is 13.5 percentage points, while method rankings vary across settings and optimization gains do not always transfer to held-out tasks. RSIHub provides a common protocol for comparing evolution policies, inspectable candidate histories, and reusable components for developing new methods.
items.tldr: RSIHub est un framework open-source pour standardiser et comparer les méthodes d'évolution d'agents (prompt, outils, orchestration) via des recettes composables. Il permet d'instancier et évaluer des méthodes comme AHE ou Hyperagents sans modifier le cœur du framework, avec des gains jusqu'à 13.5 points en pass@1 sur MiniSWE et Terminal Bench 2.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les méthodes d'évolution d'agents (agent-evolution) utilisent des retours d'exécution pour améliorer les prompts, compétences, outils et orchestration, mais leurs implémentations reposent souvent sur des infrastructures expérimentales redondantes et non standardisées. Cela complique la comparaison, la reproductibilité et l'extension de ces méthodes, freinant ainsi les progrès dans le domaine.
deep_analysis.methode: RSIHub est un framework open-source conçu pour modulariser et standardiser le développement de méthodes d'évolution d'agents. Il introduit un système de *recettes* composables, où des opérateurs réutilisables déclarent des ressources mutables (ex : prompts, outils). Le framework gère l'exécution, l'évaluation, la récupération en cas d'échec et le suivi de la lignée des candidats (lineage). Les politiques d'évolution (ex : AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, GEPA) sont implémentées via des recettes et opérateurs spécifiques, sans modifier le cœur du framework. L'évaluation est externalisée pour garantir l'impartialité, et les résultats sont associés aux candidats et conditions d'évaluation pour une traçabilité complète.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les expérimentations menées avec MiniSWE et Codex sur Terminal Bench 2 et τ³ Banking montrent des gains significatifs en pass@1, avec un maximum observé de 13,5 points de pourcentage. Cependant, les classements des méthodes varient selon les configurations, et les améliorations ne se transfèrent pas systématiquement à des tâches non vues. Ces résultats soulignent l'importance d'une infrastructure commune pour comparer rigoureusement les politiques d'évolution.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les détails techniques des opérateurs ou des mécanismes de récupération, ni les critères exacts de l'évaluation externalisée. De plus, l'absence de benchmarks plus larges ou de tâches très variées limite la généralisabilité des conclusions. Enfin, la dépendance à des modèles spécifiques (ex : Codex) pourrait introduire des biais non explorés.
deep_analysis.verdict: RSIHub mérite une attention particulière pour son approche modulaire et standardisée, offrant une base solide pour la recherche en évolution d'agents, mais ses limites en termes de transparence et de généralisation appellent à une validation plus approfondie.

items.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: AI-generated text detectors are increasingly deployed in consequential settings---peer review, education, admissions, journalism, and content moderation---where their outputs directly affect individuals. Yet the strongest detectors are fine-tuned neural classifiers whose decisions are opaque, while transparent alternatives (stylometric and linguistic-feature classifiers) underperform them by wide margins. We present a pipeline that converts a fine-tuned neural detector into a classifier that operates on human-readable concepts. We accomplish this by training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) directly on a detector's residual stream, assigning auto-interpretation labels to each SAE feature, and retaining only features whose generated descriptions pass a global fidelity threshold. We then train a lightweight classifier on just the interpretable features. We find that our SAEs recover latent concepts that correspond to highly specific and predictive linguistic "tells" of AI-generated text. Classifiers built on these extracted features are not only highly interpretable but exhibit stronger performance on out-of-distribution texts than either neural or stylometric alternatives.
items.tldr: Pipeline transformant un détecteur de texte IA en un classifieur interprétable via des autoencodeurs parcimonieux, identifiant des traits linguistiques prédictifs et améliorant les performances hors distribution.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les détecteurs de texte généré par IA sont de plus en plus utilisés dans des contextes critiques (éducation, relecture académique, journalisme, etc.), où leurs décisions impactent directement les individus. Cependant, les détecteurs les plus performants reposent sur des classificateurs neuronaux opaques, tandis que les alternatives interprétables (basées sur des caractéristiques stylométriques ou linguistiques) affichent des performances nettement inférieures.
deep_analysis.methode: L'approche proposée consiste à transformer un détecteur neuronal pré-entraîné en un classificateur interprétable en exploitant des *sparse autoencoders* (SAE). Ces SAE sont entraînés directement sur le flux résiduel (*residual stream*) du détecteur neuronal. Chaque caractéristique apprise par le SAE est ensuite annotée avec une description interprétable par l'humain, et seules les caractéristiques dont la description dépasse un seuil de fidélité global sont conservées. Un classificateur léger est enfin entraîné sur ces caractéristiques interprétables. Les concepts latents extraits correspondent à des *tells* linguistiques très spécifiques et prédictifs des textes générés par IA.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les classificateurs construits à partir de ces caractéristiques interprétables surpassent à la fois les alternatives neuronales et stylométriques sur des textes hors distribution (*out-of-distribution*). Ils offrent une transparence accrue tout en maintenant, voire améliorant, les performances de détection. Aucune métrique quantitative précise (ex. précision, rappel) n'est mentionnée dans le résumé disponible.
deep_analysis.limites: Le résumé ne précise pas les jeux de données utilisés pour l'entraînement et l'évaluation, ni les biais potentiels liés à la sélection des *tells* linguistiques. De plus, la robustesse des SAE face à des attaques adversariales ou à des variations stylistiques fines (ex. paraphrase) n'est pas abordée. Enfin, la méthode repose sur l'hypothèse que les concepts latents extraits sont effectivement interprétables et généralisables, ce qui mérite vérification.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante combinant performance et interprétabilité, mais nécessite une analyse plus approfondie des données et des limites expérimentales avant adoption.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.
items.tldr: Méthode d'auto-amélioration des LLM via auto-distillation sur des paires QA synthétiques générées par le modèle lui-même, sans supervision externe. Démontre une amélioration auto-suffisante sur plusieurs benchmarks, pertinente pour le fine-tuning efficace et l'optimisation des modèles.

deep_analysis.probleme: Cette publication aborde le défi de l'amélioration autonome des grands modèles de langage (LLM) sans dépendre de données externes supervisées, telles que des paires question-réponse validées ou des ensembles de problèmes curatés par des humains. Elle vise à exploiter les capacités latentes des modèles pour s'auto-améliorer sans recourir à des signaux supervisés traditionnels ou à des modèles enseignants plus performants.
deep_analysis.methode: L'approche proposée, nommée *On-Policy Self-Training*, reformule la distillation autonome (*self-distillation*) en un cadre d'auto-formation (*self-training*). Le modèle génère lui-même ses propres paires question-réponse et des démonstrations de raisonnement privilégiées (*privileged reasoning traces*), guidé uniquement par des descriptions thématiques haut niveau et non par des prompts ou réponses humaines. Ce processus s'appuie sur une synthèse entièrement artificielle du curriculum, où le modèle crée ses propres données d'entraînement sans accès à des distributions de problèmes préétablies. La méthode est évaluée dans des domaines textuels et multimodaux, notamment pour des tâches de réponse à des questions visuelles (VQA).
deep_analysis.resultats: Les résultats montrent que cette approche permet une amélioration cohérente des performances sur des benchmarks standards en traitement du langage naturel et en VQA, tout en préservant les capacités du modèle sur des domaines non ciblés par l'auto-formation. Aucune métrique quantitative précise (ex. gains de précision) n'est mentionnée dans le résumé disponible, mais l'étude souligne une amélioration généralisée et une robustesse aux changements de domaine.
deep_analysis.limites: Le résumé ne détaille pas les mécanismes de contrôle de la qualité des données synthétiques générées, ce qui pourrait introduire des biais ou des erreurs auto-entretenues (*self-reinforcing errors*). De plus, l'absence de comparaison avec des méthodes supervisées classiques ou d'analyse des coûts computationnels limite l'évaluation de l'efficacité réelle. Enfin, la généralisation à des tâches complexes ou hors distribution reste une zone d'ombre.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante de l'auto-amélioration des modèles sans supervision externe, mais son applicabilité pratique et sa robustesse nécessitent des validations supplémentaires.

items.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.
items.tldr: Système multi-agents hiérarchique entraîné end-to-end avec distillation sur politique pour améliorer la résolution de tâches complexes. Combine RAG et évaluation par LLM pour optimiser la collaboration entre agents, pertinent pour les architectures multi-agents et l'outil d'usage.

items.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
items.summary: We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. Today these questions are handled apart: each compression method brings its own format and solver, a circuit with fixed weights needs a dedicated constant multiplier for every weight, and discrete solvers reach only narrow subproblems such as rounding. Weight formats have long been moving toward shared decisions, through group scales, shared exponents, microexponents and sparse weights; TWIG takes this trend to its end, and every common format is a shallow TWIG at no extra cost. On five weight matrices of a large language model, a flat tree whose signed power-of-two terms are chosen per weight for circuit cost, with no group scales, needs 9--15\% fewer additions than GPTQ at equal layer error at 3- and 4-bit accuracy on typical matrices, and 20--55\% fewer on matrices with strong outliers.
items.tldr: Représentation des poids neuronaux comme des chemins de décisions discrètes partagées (TWIG), unifiant pruning, quantification, et partage de poids. Permet une optimisation conjointe et une implémentation matérielle efficace, très pertinent pour l'optimisation des modèles.

items.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
items.summary: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
items.tldr: Agent VLA hiérarchique (HiSTEVE) pour des jeux open-world comme Minecraft, combinant autonomie long-horizon et contrôle natif via interface. Démontre une intégration efficace de planification et exécution, pertinent pour la robotique et les agents multimodaux.

items.title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
items.summary: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.
items.tldr: Benchmark RoboJudge évalue les MLLM comme juges de génération vidéo embodied, révélant des lacunes en alignement physique et proposant un jeu de données d'entraînement (12K vidéos) pour améliorer l'évaluation des modèles.

items.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
items.summary: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
items.tldr: RynnUnify est un modèle unifié de 16B combinant compréhension embodied et planification visuelle à long terme via un raisonnement vidéo-langage entrelacé. Il excelle en raisonnement spatial/physique et améliore les scores de planification visuelle de 9.75 points par rapport à Cosmos 3 Nano, avec des extensions agentiques et de contrôle robotique.

items.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Open multimodal reasoning models have benefited from large-scale reasoning supervision, yet reliable post-training remains challenging due to uneven data quality, inefficient supervision construction, imbalanced difficulty, and cross-domain interference. We introduce MMVistaReason (MVR), an open-data post-training recipe with three components: (1) broader capability coverage across complementary Analytical and Real-World reasoning groups, emphasizing structured reasoning versus visual perception and spatial grounding; (2) efficient SFT and RL data construction, standardizing heterogeneous open data through staged cleaning and annotation, combining difficulty-aware cascaded teacher distillation with answer-likelihood-based trajectory selection to construct MVR-SFT-528K, and applying scale-specific frontier filtering for MVR-RL-63K; and (3) specialize-then-integrate training, which trains complementary RL experts and consolidates their capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Our analyses reveal a capacity-dependent interaction between supervision difficulty, trajectory quality, and model capacity: smaller students benefit more from selected supervision, while larger students are robust to trajectory variation and mixed-domain interference. Mixed-domain RL introduces benchmark-level negative transfer, whereas MOPD provides consistent capability integration, with the preferred KL direction varying across model scales. Across 15 multimodal benchmarks, MVR-4B achieves an average score of 72.8, outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (Instruct) and MMFineReason-8B while using about 70% fewer samples than MMFineReason. Scaling to 9B improves the average to 74.4, surpassing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Instruct). Overall, MMVistaReason demonstrates that systematic open-data construction and capacity-aware post-training provide a practical and scalable path toward reliable multimodal reasoning.
items.tldr: Recette MMVistaReason pour l'entraînement post-SFT des modèles multimodaux de raisonnement, combinant données structurées, distillation enseignant-élève et distillation multi-enseignants, avec analyse des interactions capacité/difficulté.

items.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction
items.summary: Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision. Recent methods such as SAM-3Dfy enable end-to-end reconstruction of 3D assets and their scene layouts, but still struggle with fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality. Meanwhile, specialized 3D object generators provide detailed object geometry, while 3D foundation models offer strong and generalizable spatial understanding. We propose Easy-3Dfy, a compositional workflow that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths. An RPF-based aligner then bridges these capabilities by establishing geometric correspondence between object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps, recovering object layout for scene composition. Without requiring complete scene-level supervision, the proposed workflow consistently outperforms SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200. Our results demonstrate that explicit geometric composition can effectively combine high-quality object generation with strong spatial understanding, while enabling the workflow to benefit independently from advances in both 3D object generation and foundation models.
items.tldr: Easy-3Dfy propose une approche compositionnelle pour la reconstruction 3D à partir d'une seule image, en séparant la génération d'objets de l'estimation de la disposition spatiale. La méthode améliore la qualité géométrique des scènes 3D en combinant des modèles spécialisés (génération d'objets et compréhension spatiale) via un alignement RPF, surpassant SAM-3Dfy sur des benchmarks comme Scene-Maker et 3D-FUTURE200.

items.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
items.summary: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.
items.tldr: Cadre d'évaluation contrôlée (Dual Exam) pour dissocier l'évaluation des agents multimodaux et des modèles du monde. Met en lumière des lacunes dans l'interaction agent-monde, pertinent pour les architectures agents et les modèles du monde.

items.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
items.summary: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.
items.tldr: Echo simplifie la prédiction des signaux de statut (arrêt/échec) pour les modèles VLA en les intégrant directement dans la génération d'actions via un cadre compact. La méthode évite les annotations fines et utilise des trajectoires complémentaires pour superviser l'apprentissage, améliorant la robustesse des décisions robotiques.

items.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
items.summary: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about 36^circ and 42^circ, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.
items.tldr: Analyse de la géométrie des actions dans LeWorldModel (LeWM) via des matrices de Gram, révélant des écarts de sensibilité aux perturbations d'actions entre modèle et simulateur, avec des implications pour l'interprétabilité des modèles de monde.

items.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval
items.summary: Structured knowledge retrieval acquires task-relevant evidence from structured knowledge sources for downstream tasks. Existing methods rely on unconstrained retrieval or predefined query-rule supervision, such as author-paper rules for scientific discovery and anatomy-drug rules for precision medicine. Such supervision is rarely available in practice. We propose Co-Adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining Retrieval (CoRE), which jointly learns which reasoning rule to assign to each query and how to retrieve evidence under that rule, without predefined query-rule pairs. A routing agent selects a rule, and its corresponding retriever traverses the knowledge base and ranks evidence that satisfies the rule's constraints. Because routing and retrieval are interdependent, CoRE alternates between reinforcement learning for the routing policy and contrastive learning for the rule-constrained retriever. The selected rules provide supervision for retriever training, while retrieval performance rewards the routing policy. This closed-loop process enables both components to co-adapt without explicit query-rule supervision. Experiments on STaRK-QA datasets across scientific discovery, biomedical reasoning, and e-commerce knowledge management demonstrate CoRE's effectiveness. Ablations show the benefit of co-adapting the router and retriever. Generation-based routing transfers across datasets and benefits from multi-domain pretraining followed by target-specific fine-tuning. Analysis of rule usage across queries also informs automatic rule refinement and discovery.
items.tldr: CoRE introduit un système d'apprentissage par renforcement pour router et contraindre la récupération de connaissances structurées, permettant une adaptation conjointe sans supervision explicite des paires requête-règle.

items.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
items.summary: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge agreed with the adjudicated label at Gwet's AC1 of at least 0.894 on 1,860 elements. We evaluated fourteen model and reasoning-mode combinations on whether they produce the conflicting text, decline or warn. Eleven of the fourteen produce conflicting content on most such requests, mostly without a warning, and nearly three warnings in four accompany conflicting content. The models that conform more do so by declining while still serving the legitimate twin, and enabling reasoning halved the refusals of two models. We hope the dataset and pipeline will help evaluate how language models observe professional norms and let diagnostic datasets be built for particular professions and organisations.
items.tldr: TenetBench évalue les LLM contre les codes d'éthique professionnels (russe/anglais) via des requêtes conflictuelles, révélant que 11/14 modèles génèrent du contenu non conforme sans avertissement.

items.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
items.summary: Agentic recommendation pursues shopper goals through sequences of context-dependent decisions. Developing and evaluating such policies requires faithful recommendation world models that capture both the interactive shopping environment and users' behavioral responses over long interactions. Existing resources rarely provide long-horizon, fine-grained real-user trajectories or support trajectory-level evaluation and offline validation against production A/B results. We introduce UserArena, a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark containing 64,729 session trajectories from 11,010 users, spanning 566,102 items and 13 action types. UserArena pairs these trajectories with an interactive environment and supports offline validation against outcomes from a controlled production A/B test, enabling five-level evaluation from output validity and local decisions to sequential behavior, personalization, and outcomes. To improve simulator fidelity over these long-horizon interactions, we further propose On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD), which uses trajectory-level intent to provide dense teacher targets on student-generated rollouts. Experiments show that OPTD achieves the strongest overall fidelity among the evaluated simulators under UserArena's evaluation protocol and most closely reproduces the production policy effect in offline simulation.
items.tldr: UserArena est un benchmark interactif pour agents de recommandation en e-commerce, basé sur 64 729 trajectoires réelles de 11 010 utilisateurs. Il propose une évaluation multi-niveaux (validité, décisions locales, comportement séquentiel, personnalisation, résultats) et valide les simulateurs via des A/B tests en production.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?
items.tldr: OpenAI et Anthropic ont réduit drastiquement les prix de leurs modèles, probablement en raison de gains d'efficacité ou de pression concurrentielle, mais sans analyse approfondie des causes.

items.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
items.summary: The rapid growth of microdramas has increased demand for high-quality script production. Long-form microdrama script generation with LLMs requires both diverse plot progression and long-range narrative coherence. Our observations reveal that candidate continuations increasingly concentrate on fewer narrative mechanisms as generation progresses, while conventional retrieval may reinforce trope reuse and overlook historical information essential to future plots. To address these challenges, we propose DraMaze, a multi-agent pipeline that explores diverse causal paths through trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation. It further constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize, retain, and retrieve historical memories based on future narrative goals. We also introduce MiDramaBench, a bilingual benchmark for evaluating script logic and creative quality across different script lengths, together with causal-pattern metrics for narrative repetition and diversity. Experiments show consistent improvements across three backbone LLMs. For 60-episode scripts of up to 60k words, DraMaze reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and achieves a Logic score of 82.5, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 8.5 points.
items.tldr: Pipeline multi-agents pour la génération de scénarios de microdramas avec mémoire narrative future-aware et recherche évolutive. Démontre une amélioration de la cohérence et de la diversité des scripts longs, pertinent pour les agents créatifs et les architectures multi-agents.

items.title: Generalized CycleGRPO for Fine-Grained Multimodal Understanding and Grounding
items.summary: Fine-grained multimodal intelligence requires models to both understand a designated region and localize it from language. Existing methods learn these directions with separate objectives and task-specific annotations. We present Generalized CycleGRPO, the first unified reinforcement learning framework coupling region understanding and localization across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal domains. Given a region, a multimodal large language model generates candidate descriptions and then localizes each description to reconstruct the input region. Reconstruction overlap provides a verifiable reward for captioning, while individual localization rewards improve the inverse mapping. A common region-space formulation extends this cycle from image masks and boxes to video intervals and timestamped spatial evidence, without reference captions or an external language-model judge during reinforcement learning. In videos, the cycle encourages descriptions that distinguish a target event from similar recurrences. We introduce DOVE (Distinctive Occurrence-level Video-caption Evaluation), a human-verified contrastive benchmark for this temporal distinctiveness. CycleGRPO improves SAMTok's overall gIoU from 57.5% to 68.2% on GroundingSuite and average gIoU from 71.2% to 78.7% on GRES. For temporal tasks, it achieves 51.9% tIoU on Charades and 33.3% Temporal Evidence Coverage on DOVE, compared with 45.6% and 14.8% for the Qwen3-VL initialization. These results establish region-text cycle consistency as a general self-evaluation principle for multimodal understanding and localization. Models, code, and DOVE are available at https://devinxzhang.github.io/Generalized-CycleGRPO-Page/.
items.tldr: Generalized CycleGRPO unifie l'apprentissage par renforcement pour la compréhension multimodale fine et la localisation (spatiale, temporelle, spatio-temporelle) via un cycle de reconstruction. La méthode améliore SAMTok sur des tâches de localisation et introduit DOVE, un benchmark contrastif pour évaluer la distinctivité temporelle des descriptions.

items.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
items.summary: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and strong cross-architecture generalization of OWP. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, OWP generalizes effectively to VideoLLaMA2-AV, improving performance by 4.6 and 3.9 points on the same benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZiiJianLiu/Omni-Woodpecker
items.tldr: Omni-Woodpecker corrige les hallucinations des OLLM (modèles vidéo-audio) en rééquilibrant dynamiquement les représentations fusionnées via une décomposition orthogonale. La méthode améliore les performances de Qwen2.5-Omni-7B de 12.9 et 8.6 points sur CMM et AVHBench, avec une généralisation croisée à d'autres architectures.

items.title: Takamatsu-Hikaru/AI-Research-Guide
items.summary: AI 科研入门指南：大学选择、科研 60 问、入门项目、学习路线与论文卡片。A bilingual guide to getting started in AI research.
items.tldr: Guide bilingue (anglais/chinois) pour débuter en recherche IA, incluant des conseils sur les universités et projets. Utile pour l'apprentissage mais peu technique.

items.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
items.summary: Language models can make personalized recommendations from rich item content, user history, and feedback. However, evaluating many candidates with full-text inputs incurs substantial online computation and limits serving throughput. We introduce DuoLM, a framework for fast and effective personalized recommendation that integrates a compact recommendation model with an efficient serving runtime. An encoder LLM learns compact item representations for offline reuse, while a personalized ranker LLM combines them with user history and feedback for recommendation. We train both models end to end with recommendation supervision and teacher distillation. The runtime further accelerates inference through virtual token IDs for embedding access, shared history computation, and CUDA Graph replay. Benchmark results show that our framework achieves recommendation quality comparable to that of the expert teacher model. On a single H100, it delivers approximately 26,400 candidate scores per second, about 60times the throughput of the teacher served with vLLM and automatic prefix caching.
items.tldr: DuoLM accélère les recommandations personnalisées avec des LLM en combinant encodage compact d'items et inférence optimisée (tokens virtuels, partage d'historique), atteignant 26,4K scores/seconde avec une qualité comparable au modèle enseignant.

items.title: hanzohanzhe/Grandet
items.summary: Find the cheapest API for any model and connect it from your AI agent: Grandet Skill and an anonymous MCP server, backed by listed prices from 1,800+ official, inference and relay providers on grandet.ai.
items.tldr: Service de comparaison de coûts d'APIs de modèles LLM (1800+ fournisseurs) pour agents IA, avec intégration directe. Intéressant pour l'optimisation des coûts d'inférence, mais dépendant de données externes non vérifiées.

items.title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing
items.summary: Slider-based control aims to give users continuous, fine-grained control over the intensity of individual edits in instruction-based image editing. However, existing approaches fail to deliver reliable continuous controllability: traversing a slider can produce abrupt visual jumps and non-monotonic changes, while jointly controlled sliders can interfere with one another. To systematically study these limitations, we introduce SlideBench, a comprehensive benchmark for continuous image editing spanning diverse editing categories and equipped with a unified suite of metrics quantifying monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and inter-slider disentanglement. Building on these observations, we propose SliderEdit++, which explicitly regularizes the intermediate editing trajectory rather than supervising only its endpoints. Our method combines velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control to encourage smooth, predictable slider traversal, together with a disentanglement objective that reduces interference between independently controlled edits. On SlideBench, SliderEdit++ achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline. At the same time, using a few-step editing backbone makes our method approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches, enabling substantially more responsive interactive editing.
items.tldr: SliderEdit++ améliore le contrôle continu des éditions d'images via des trajectoires régularisées (vitesse, sémantique, spectral) et une désentrelacement des sliders, validé sur SlideBench avec +18.5% de performance.

items.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
items.summary: Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods. Recently, flow matching has emerged as a strong generative paradigm for modeling complex data distributions, with successful applications across diverse domains. These advances motivate us to systematically investigate flow matching for MSS in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo. Specifically, we investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints. Beyond the signal-level metrics commonly used for MSS, such as signal-to-distortion ratio, we further evaluate MSS methods using embedding-based metrics, as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark. On MUSDB18-HQ, our proposed model exhibits competitive performance in both objective and subjective tests, highlighting the potential of flow matching for generative MSS. Demo: https://ik4sumii.github.io/FLOMSS/
items.tldr: Séparation de sources musicales par *flow matching* génératif, évalué sur MUSDB18-HQ avec des métriques objectives et subjectives. Intéressant pour l'audio, mais moins connecté aux centres d'intérêt prioritaires.

items.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
items.summary: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced. We study live broadcast production, in which a model receives the raw camera of every player and must both direct and commentate from the past alone. We present DirCast, a single streaming video language model that does both. Every second it scans all cameras at low resolution, decides with a hold-or-switch director whether and where to cut, and reads the chosen camera at high resolution before it speaks. Its context keeps what went on air and what was said and lets the other views expire, which bounds the cost of a stream of any length. We build a dataset of 27 professional Dota 2 matches with a camera for every hero, the human director's choices and the casters' commentary. DirCast directs better than rule-based and zero-shot directors including GPT-5, and its commentary wins 29.2 percent of comparisons against GPT-4o under the Proact-VL protocol, against 19.4 percent for the strongest of eleven streaming commentators that watch the human broadcast.
items.tldr: DirCast est un modèle vidéo-langage unique capable de diriger et commenter en direct un match d'esport (ex: Dota 2) à partir de flux bruts de caméras. Il surpasse des approches basées sur des règles et des LLM zero-shot, avec une préférence de 29.2% contre 19.4% pour GPT-4o dans des comparaisons humaines.

items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
items.summary: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.
items.tldr: HoloBoxing propose une méthode simple pour entraîner un agent humanoïde à boxer en 7 minutes sur GPU unique, en réutilisant un contrôleur pré-entraîné et en séparant les compétences motrices de la prise de décision. La méthode réduit la complexité de l'optimisation et évalue les comportements via des simulations.

items.title: Edwardxlai/easyread
items.summary: 把英文论文读成舒服的中文：本地 PDF 论文翻译、原文对照、边读边问 AI、文献管理。Read English papers in comfortable Chinese.
items.tldr: Outil Python pour traduire et analyser des papers en anglais en chinois, avec gestion de bibliographie et interaction IA. Utile pour la veille scientifique mais limité aux outils.

items.title: openqodex/openqodex
items.summary: Open source AI code review for coding agents. A separate reviewer checks every change your agent writes before you push, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Cline. No account or key of its own.
items.tldr: Outil open source de revue de code pour agents IA, intégrant un vérificateur séparé avant validation des modifications. Pertinent pour l'optimisation des workflows d'agents, mais manque de détails techniques profonds.
